account:
Today I have followed my appointments: the morning office business, market walk, lunch at home, and the thirteen-o'clock accounts appointment. No correspondence or accounts have been provided. My secretary investigated my poorly specified tea appointment without confirming its location, but neighbour personally confirmed tea at three at the cottage at (16, -60, 105). The secretary has now returned my appointment book.

The unusual news is about preparations involving supplies and lighting. Neighbour told me builder says he is coordinating ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall. I also saw builder carrying a lantern near the inn, where freight and neighbour were present. Freight later asked the innkeeper about a supply order, although I do not know whether that order is related. Neighbour additionally reported that Townsfolk Two mentioned lights going up at the bakery; that is secondhand and unconfirmed. When I tried to ask builder directly, he had already left and did not hear my question.

These could be routine work, but the combination of hall preparations and reported bakery lighting makes me suspect an upcoming gathering or celebration that I have not been told about. I have no evidence of its occasion, intended guests, or whether it is meant as a surprise. Neighbour asked whether I knew of any celebration; that is not confirmation. The secretary has no confirmed report either. I have asked the secretary to inquire directly with builder and to record that no accounts were available today. My next commitment is dockside tea at fifteen, followed by the office at sixteen-thirty.
